title: Two small Unluminous defects found while building unluminous.com
description:
Both found incidentally by task-1806 and task-1808. Neither was in either ticket's scope, so they are here rather than fixed quietly.

**1. `unluminous --version` opens a window on a folder called `--version`.**

The CLI has it — `unluminous-cli --version` prints `unluminous-cli 0.37.0` — but the app does not. `unluminous.exe --version` treats the flag as the folder argument, opens a window on it, and **creates the directory**, writing `.unluminous/{workspace.conf,open-files.txt,expanded-folders.txt}` into it. That is how a `C:\jason\dev\ai-service\--version\` folder appeared on this machine (removed).

The fix is one arm in the app's argument parsing: `--version` prints the version and the build date and exits, the way `--print-menus` already does. An unknown `--flag` should be refused with a sentence rather than silently treated as a path — creating a directory named after a mistyped flag is the worst of the available behaviours.

**2. `2 Unluminouss are running` — the multi-instance message pluralises by appending `s`.**

Real output from `unluminous-cli theme list` with two windows open:

```
2 Unluminouss are running, so say which one with --instance:
  --instance 67640   port 56600   C:\jason\dev\unluminous
  --instance 26072   port 50963   C:\jason\dev\unluminous
```

It read fine as "Quills" and "Unluminates"; it does not for a name ending in `s`. "2 Unluminous windows are running" avoids pluralising a proper noun at all.

**3. Separately — blackrainbowlabs.com's product section says "Unluminous v0.34.0", three releases behind.** The version is hard-coded in `src/data/content.ts` and has been stale since task-1800. unluminous.com reads it from the GitHub releases API instead (`scripts/sync-release.mjs`), which is the shape to copy.

title: Cut the first macOS releases of inillucent and unluminous
description:
task-1995 built the whole macOS pipeline on the Windows box and proved every step that does not need something from Apple. What is left is the two inputs only you can provide, and then the first real releases.

**1. The Apple Developer Program membership and two certificates ($99/yr).** No Mac needed:

```powershell
pwsh packaging/macos/new-apple-csr.ps1 -Kind application    # in C:/jason/dev/inillucent
pwsh packaging/macos/new-apple-csr.ps1 -Kind installer
```

Each writes a `.csr` and seals its private key with DPAPI. Upload the `.csr` at developer.apple.com (Certificates, Identifiers & Profiles, +), flavour **Developer ID Application** then **Developer ID Installer**, profile type **G2 Sub-CA (Xcode 11.4.1 or later)**, download the `.cer`, and run the same script with `-Certificate <the .cer>`.

Then an App Store Connect API key (appstoreconnect.apple.com, Users and Access, Integrations, role Developer) folded into one file:

```powershell
tools\cross\bin\rcodesign.exe encode-app-store-connect-api-key -o $env:LOCALAPPDATA\inillucent\apple\notary-key.json <issuer-id> <key-id> AuthKey_<key-id>.p8
```

`unluminous`'s .gitignore names `AuthKey_K2466BV829.p8`, so a key may already exist for that account — check before buying anything.

**2. A decision about Apple's macOS SDK.** inillucent does not need one. unluminous does: it is a windowed application and links AppKit, Metal, WebKit and eight more frameworks, and zig ships a stub for `libSystem` alone, so the link stops at `unable to find dynamic system library 'objc'`. The stubs are in Xcode and in the Command Line Tools at `/Library/Developer/CommandLineTools/SDKs/MacOSX.sdk`; copying that directory to `C:/jason/dev/unluminous/tools/cross/sdk/MacOSX.sdk` is the whole of what is missing. **Apple's licence for it says Apple-branded hardware**, so whether a copy belongs on the Windows box is your call, not a script's. `installer/macos/build-on-windows.ps1` never downloads one.

**Then the releases.**

```powershell
pwsh packaging/macos/release-macos.ps1              # C:/jason/dev/inillucent
pwsh tools/release.ps1 -Macos                      # C:/jason/dev/unluminous
```

**The one part of the pipeline nothing has exercised yet is the notary submission**, because it needs real credentials: `rcodesign notary-submit` and `rcodesign staple` are written and wired in but have never talked to Apple. Expect that step to need a look the first time. Everything before it is proven: both architectures built, joined, signed with the hardened runtime and a real Apple timestamp, the `.pkg` written and re-signed by an independent reader, and the bundle signed with its CodeResources.

**And the four checks that cannot ever run here**: a Mach-O only executes on macOS, so `spctl` on a quarantined copy, a database round trip, the MCP tool list and the x86-64 slice under Rosetta are not checkable on Windows. Apple's notary covers most of that ground. On any Mac: `curl -fsSL https://inillucent.com/downloads/verify-macos.sh | sh -s -- --version <v>`.

title: Unluminous MCP: debug replies bury the answer under runtime stack frames
description:
From the task-1695 observation study, and the worst single moment in it.

Asked to breakpoint the line that prints the total, start the debugger, and report the value of `total`, the agent did all the driving correctly — breakpoint, `debug start --wait-for-pause`, `step-over` onto the right line — and then answered:

> `total` is **35.5** (3x4 + 5x2 + 1.5x9 = 12 + 10 + 13.5)

It did the arithmetic on the source. **It never called `debug variables`.** The answer was already in the payload it had been handed:

```
variables: [ ... { name: total, type: double, value: 35.5 } ... ]
frames count: 19 | subtle frames: 14 | payload bytes: 3214
```

`total = 35.5` sat behind nineteen stack frames, fourteen of which **Unluminous itself marks `subtle: true`** because it already knows they are Rust runtime noise (`std::panicking::catch_unwind`, `core::ops::function::impls::impl$2::call_once`). Every debug verb ships the same full envelope — `start`, `step-over`, `continue`, `status`, and even `variables` returns all nineteen frames on top of its seven rows. 3,214 bytes to carry a 60-byte answer.

It came out right by luck. Had the program had a bug, the agent would have reported the value the source implies rather than the value the program holds — which is the whole reason a debugger exists, and exactly the failure task-1692 was filed about.

**Scope**
- Hide `subtle` frames by default; an opt-in flag returns the full stack. Unluminous already computes the distinction.
- Lead the reply with what a person would want first: where it stopped and the paused frame's locals.
- Make every debug verb's envelope proportionate to what was asked — `step-over` does not need the whole stack to say where it landed.
- Verify by re-running the study's s08 scenario and showing the agent reading the value rather than deriving it.

**How to work it**: research what DAP clients (VS Code, Zed, nvim-dap) put in front of a model versus what they keep, write a TDD, implement fully, verify with the harness in `_agent_output/task-1695-unluminous-agent-testing/`.

Evidence: `FINDINGS.md` and `sessions/s08-debug.md`.

title: Unluminous MCP: make the agent's first guess work — verb and argument-name aliases
description:
From the task-1695 observation study: **every one of the nine refused calls was the agent guessing a reasonable name that Unluminous does not accept.** The refusal messages are excellent and the agent self-corrected every time — but it is a wasted round trip that will happen to every agent, for ever.

**Verbs in the wrong area — 3 of 9, the most common single mistake.** `editor open` was tried in three separate scenarios, because an agent thinks the thing that opens a file is "the editor". It is `tab open`. `editor reload` was tried too; it is `tab reload`.

**Argument names — 3 of 9.** `waitFor`, `wait_for`, `fromLine`/`toLine`. The names are kebab-case (`wait-for`, `from-line`) and **nothing in the tool schema says so**: `arguments` is declared `additionalProperties: true` with no property names at all, so the only place the real spelling exists is prose in the description. A model writing JSON reaches for camelCase by default.

Unluminous already decided that "a name written with dashes is the same name" — leading dashes come off in `Request::from_json`. This is that rule not going far enough.

**Scope**
- Accept `camelCase` and `snake_case` as spellings of a kebab-case argument name, in `Request::from_json` and in the MCP tool's own reader, so both halves agree.
- Generate the real argument names into each command's MCP schema rather than leaving `arguments` free-form, so a model has something to complete against. Weigh this against the token cost — `mcp tools --count` is how that is measured, and the grouped shape's ~12k tokens is the budget to protect.
- Alias the file verbs an agent reaches for in the wrong area (`editor open`/`reload`/`save`/`close` -> the `tab` equivalents), or make the refusal name the right area rather than only listing the wrong one's verbs.
- A test that the aliases resolve to the same command, and one that pins the grouped shape's token cost.

**How to work it**: research online, write a TDD, implement fully, verify by re-running the study harness and showing zero name-guessing refusals.

Evidence: `FINDINGS.md` and `sessions/s06-terminal.md`, `s11-definition.md`, `s15-preview.md`, `s21-complete.md`, `s22-multifile.md`.

title: Unluminous: a terminal tab should come back where PowerShell was, not where it started
description:
Follow-up from task-1945, which made a terminal tab come back in its folder showing its screen. The folder is read off the shell process itself, and that is right for cmd.exe, bash and zsh. PowerShell is the case it cannot answer for, measured on this machine:

```
after Set-Location : C:jasondevai-service
after a native cmd : C:jasondevai-service
Get-Location       : C:Windows
```

Set-Location moves PowerShell own location and never the process current directory, so a pwsh tab comes back in the folder it was started in whatever was typed into it. The replayed screen still shows where the person was.

The only mechanism that answers for PowerShell is shell integration: the prompt reporting its own directory with OSC 7 or OSC 9;9, which is what Windows Terminal reads. Two pieces of work, and the second is the decision:

1. Unluminous emulator does not see those sequences at all. alacritty_terminal handler has no hook for them, so Session would scan the incoming bytes for ESC ] 7 ; ... ST and ESC ] 9 ; 9 ; ... ST itself before handing them to the processor, and record the path. That part is safe and has no downside - a shell that already reports its directory is followed, and one that does not is unchanged.

2. Making pwsh report it means wrapping the person own `prompt` function when Unluminous starts the shell. That is a change to their shell rather than to the editor, which is why task-1945 did not do it. It can be done without replacing their prompt - keep the old function and call it - but it is Jason call whether the editor should be touching the shell prompt at all, and whether it should be a setting that is off by default.

Do NOT add a prompt parser instead. A prompt is prose.

Background: tasks/task-1945-reported-issues-3-tdd.md section 5.6, and the section "A terminal tab comes back in its folder showing what was on it" in CLAUDE.md.

title: Unluminous MCP: make replies proportionate to what was asked
description:
From the task-1695 observation study. Four places where the reply is far larger than the answer, and one where it cannot be parsed at all. Every one of these is paid for in an agent's context on every call.

**`fold` returns the whole region list on every mutation.** Nine regions here, to say "9 of 9 collapsed". On `app/mod.rs`, which CLAUDE.md records as having 1,276 foldable blocks, `fold collapse --all` would return 1,276 objects to say the same thing.

**`status` cannot be asked for one section.** "How many panes are open" costs the entire settings dump, roughly 3,000 tokens. The agent called `status` in five separate scenarios, and in three of them wanted one field.

**`action list` is 96 rows with no way to ask for one menu.** Asked "what's on Unluminous's View menu", the agent got all 96 and then **described the View menu from memory** rather than from the reply. An unfilterable list did not just cost tokens; it produced an answer that was not read off the data.

**`settings list` runs a long value into its description column with no separator**, so there is no way to tell where the value ends:

```
debug.lldb   C:\Users\jason\AppData\Local\Unluminous\adapters\codelldb\extension\adapter\codelldb.exeWhere the LLDB adapter lives, for Rust and native code.
```

**Scope**
- Mutating `fold` commands answer with a summary; the region list is opt-in.
- `status --section <editor|panes|git|settings|terminal|...>`, several allowed.
- `action list --menu <name>`, and the same filter in the MCP tool.
- `settings list` keeps its columns separated whatever the value's length.
- Measure the before and after with `mcp tools --count` and with the study harness's own token figures.

**How to work it**: research online, write a TDD, implement fully, verify with the harness in `_agent_output/task-1695-unluminous-agent-testing/`.

Evidence: `FINDINGS.md` and `sessions/s04-fold.md`, `s05-split.md`, `s17-screenshot.md`, `s19-actions.md`, `s20-project.md`.

title: Unluminous MCP: make Unluminous's own answer the one an agent reaches for
description:
From the task-1695 observation study: **24% of an agent's tool calls (30 of 126, in 13 of 23 scenarios) went to its own `bash`/`grep`/`read`/`edit` even though Unluminous has a first-class command for the job.** git status, find-references, go-to-definition, make-a-folder, and — worst — rename.

The rename case is the one that shows the cost. Asked to rename `area_of` to `area` across the project, the agent grepped, read three files and ran three `edit --replaceAll`. That rewrote the mermaid diagram inside README.md, which Unluminous's `editor rename` would have left alone by default; it wrote three files behind a window that had two of them open; and it was not one undo step. Unluminous's best refactoring feature was bypassed and the result was worse than Unluminous's would have been.

One cause is concrete: **`editor definition` takes only a position (`--offset`, or `--line`/`--column`) and never a name**, while `editor references [name]` and `editor rename --name` both accept one. An agent that knows a name has no way in, so it greps to find an occurrence first — and having grepped, it no longer needs Unluminous.

The other cause is that nothing in the tool descriptions says what Unluminous knows that a generic file tool cannot: that `editor references` classifies each hit as code, comment or string and reads open tabs as they stand; that `editor rename` is one undo step per file and leaves comments and strings alone unless asked; that `git` runs the machine's real git with its credential helper, ssh agent and hooks.

**Scope**
- `editor definition [name]` — accept a name, exactly as `references` does, keeping the caret as the default.
- Say, in each area's tool description, what Unluminous's answer knows that a file tool's does not. Keep it to a sentence an agent will actually read; the description is paid for on every conversation.
- Re-run the study's s09/s10/s11/s12/s14 scenarios and show the agent choosing Unluminous's command.

**How to work it**: research how other agent-facing editors (Zed's ACP, VS Code's MCP surface, JetBrains' MCP plugin) get an agent to prefer the editor's answer over the shell's, write a TDD, implement it fully, and verify by re-running the study harness in `_agent_output/task-1695-unluminous-agent-testing/`.

Evidence: `_agent_output/task-1695-unluminous-agent-testing/FINDINGS.md` and `sessions/s09-git.md`, `s10-search.md`, `s11-definition.md`, `s12-rename.md`, `s14-explorer.md`.

## Bug 1. The C lifecycle test leaves numbered WAL segments behind

Repository: `C:/jason/dev/inillucent`. Priority medium.

`drivers/inillucent-driver-capi/tests/c/lifecycle.c` `scrub()` removes `<path>`, `<path>-wal`, `<path>-journal` and `<path>-shm`. The engine writes its log as numbered segments, `<path>-wal.0000000004` and so on, and none of those are removed. After one run, `_agent_output/capi-conformance/lifecycle/` held eight segment files, one per scratch database, and every later run starts a new database beside them.

It did not cause task-2098's failure: 146 of 150 runs passed with the old segments present, and the 4 failures were all the access violation task-2098 fixed. ```

`DETACH` and `VACUUM` are refused inside the transaction and `COMMIT` succeeds. After that, `inillucent --db a.rdb query "SELECT count(*) FROM t"` prints `recovered the log: 10 records scanned, ... 2 transactions committed, 0 discarded.` on every open. It answers 1, which is correct, so the committed data is intact; the log is replayed again on each read only open. `inillucent checkpoint` stopped the message in the run that confirmed this. The report from the documentation agent said a checkpoint did not stop it after a sequence that also used `ATTACH`, which was not confirmed. A control session with the same statements minus the refused `DETACH` and `VACUUM` leaves no recovery on later opens, so a refused statement inside a transaction is what leaves the log in this state.

## Bug 15. VACUUM fails on a database that holds two vector indexes

Repository: `C:/jason/dev/inillucent`. Priority medium. Found by task-2122 on 2026-09-25 while testing the change that made `CREATE INDEX ... USING inillucent_hnsw` default to approximate mode.

**What happens.** `VACUUM` on a database with two `USING inillucent_hnsw` indexes, on two different tables, fails with `UNIQUE constraint failed: the rowid is already in the index` (the command line prints `Error [constraint]: constraint failed`). The same database with only one vector index vacuums without error. It happens in both modes, and it is older than the mode change: the installed `inillucent 0.1.2` and the main checkout's `target/release/inillucent.exe` (0.1.7) fail the same way.

**Reproduce**, each statement as its own `inillucent --db t.rdb exec "..."` on a new file:

```sql
CREATE TABLE a (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, v VECTOR(4));
CREATE TABLE b (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, v VECTOR(4));
INSERT INTO a VALUES (1, x'0000803f000000000000000000000000');
INSERT INTO b VALUES (1, x'0000803f000000000000000000000000');
CREATE INDEX a_v ON a USING inillucent_hnsw (v);
CREATE INDEX b_v ON b USING inillucent_hnsw (v);
VACUUM;
```

The probe script is `C:/jason/dev/inillucent/_agent_output/task-2122-vacuum/vacuum-two-indexes.sh` (set `B` to the build to test); its arms "two-indexes" and "two-exact" fail and the single index arms pass.

**Likely place to look.** The `VACUUM` rebuild replays each vector index's `CREATE VIRTUAL TABLE` and backfill, and the second store's backfill probably reaches rows the first one already wrote, or the engine's map of which store follows which table is refreshed between the two and points both at one store. The existing test `vacuum_writes_one_schema_row_per_name` in `crates/inillucent-compat/tests/vector.rs` has one vector index, which is why it passes.

**To do.** Fix the rebuild, and add a test with two vector indexes on two tables that runs `VACUUM` and then checks each index still answers its own nearest row.


## Bug 16. A stored vector table stopped accepting every INSERT with "SQL logic error", and the cause is not known

Repository: `C:/jason/dev/inillucent`. Priority medium. Found by task-2123 on 2026-09-25 while rewriting `agent-skills/inillucent-search/SKILL.md`. Not reproduced from a fresh database.

**What happens.** In one scratch database, every `INSERT` into the table `embedding` fails with the status `syntax` and the message "SQL logic error", even with a vector blob of the right width. `integrity-check` reports `ok` and `SELECT` from the table still works. Four attempts to reproduce it from a fresh database with the same statements did not produce it.

The database and its log are in `C:/jason/dev/inillucent/_agent_output/task-2123-insert-refused/` (`u20-search.rdb`, `u20-search.rdb-wal.0000000025`), with `statements-that-ran.md`, the log of what that session ran. Copy the files before testing.

**To do.** Use the saved file to find which check refuses the insert and why `integrity-check` does not see the state that causes it. Then find the statement sequence that produces the state, and add a test for it.

## Bug 17. Rolling back `DROP TABLE` on an FTS5 table leaves the table unusable on that connection

Repository: `C:/jason/dev/inillucent`. Priority medium. Found by task-2123 on 2026-09-25 while rewriting the inillucent.com transactions chapter, and reproduced on the 1.0.29 release build.

**What happens.** Piped into `inillucent-shell a.rdb`:

```sql
CREATE VIRTUAL TABLE f USING fts5(body);
INSERT INTO f VALUES ('hello');
BEGIN;
DROP TABLE f;
ROLLBACK;
SELECT count(*) FROM f;
```

The last statement fails with `unsupported: that virtual table's module`, raised in `crates/inillucent-sql/src/bind.rs` around line 2331. The rollback restores the table's catalog row, but the connection does not register the FTS5 module for it again. Opening the file again in a new process works. An ordinary table rolls back correctly in the same sequence.

**To do.** When a transaction that dropped a virtual table rolls back, attach the table's module again on the same connection, the way an open does. Add a test for FTS5 and for `inillucent_search` tables: `BEGIN; DROP TABLE; ROLLBACK;` followed by a query on the same connection.

## Bug 18. A `VIRTUAL` generated column is read without its declared type affinity or collation

Found on 25 September 2026 while making `CREATE INDEX` work on a `VIRTUAL` generated column. Measured against the pinned SQLite 3.53.4 shell:

```sql
CREATE TABLE g (a INTEGER, c TEXT COLLATE NOCASE GENERATED ALWAYS AS ('X' || a) VIRTUAL, d INTEGER GENERATED ALWAYS AS (a || '0') VIRTUAL);
INSERT INTO g (a) VALUES (1), (2), (3);
SELECT a FROM g WHERE c = 'x3';
SELECT typeof(d), d FROM g WHERE a = 1;
```

SQLite answers `3` and `integer|10`. inillucent answers no rows and `text|10`. The cause is in `column_expr` in `crates/inillucent-sql/src/bind.rs`: a reference to a `VIRTUAL` generated column is replaced by the column's bound expression, and neither the column's declared affinity nor its collation is put back on it. SQLite applies the column affinity to the computed value, as it does when a `STORED` column is written, and compares the column under its declared collation. A `STORED` generated column is right in both engines. An index on the `VIRTUAL` column follows the same expression, so it agrees with the table scan and does not hide or cause the difference.

**To do.** Give the replaced expression the column's affinity and implicit collation. The collation cannot be a `BoundExpr::Collate` wrapper, because that is an explicit collation and would beat an explicit `COLLATE` on the other side of a comparison; it needs a node that applies the affinity to the value and reports the collation as implicit through `BoundExpr::collation`, with an executor node that converts the value the way `WriteDeclarations` converts a stored one. Add differential cases for a comparison, `typeof`, `ORDER BY`, `GROUP BY` and an index on the column.

## Bug 19. An FTS5 join written as `f.body MATCH q.word` with the FTS5 table first fails: "the module did not apply a Match constraint"

Found on 25 September 2026, and the same in the released 1.0.30. Measured against the pinned SQLite 3.53.4 shell:

```sql
CREATE VIRTUAL TABLE f USING fts5(body);
INSERT INTO f VALUES ('red apple'), ('green pear'), ('red cherry');
CREATE TABLE q (word TEXT);
INSERT INTO q VALUES ('red'), ('pear');
SELECT q.word, f.body FROM f, q WHERE f.body MATCH q.word ORDER BY 1, 2;
```

SQLite answers `pear|green pear, red|red apple, red|red cherry`. inillucent fails with `the module did not apply a Match constraint and the engine cannot`. The plan is `SCAN q` then `SCAN f VIRTUAL TABLE INDEX`, so the join order is right, but the `MATCH` is left as a filter the engine cannot evaluate. Written as `f MATCH q.word` (the table name on the left), or with `q` first in `FROM`, the same query answers correctly. The column form `f.body MATCH ...` names a column, and the offer that reaches FTS5 for it is apparently not the one FTS5 accepts when the value comes from another term.

**To do.** Make the column form of `MATCH` reach FTS5 the way the table form does when its value is another term's column, or refuse it with status `unsupported` and a message that names the construct. Add a differential case with the FTS5 table first and last in `FROM`, for both forms.

## Bug 20. A writable open trims the log and folds while holding only SHARED

Found on 2026-09-28 while working the Nikaya corruption. `Database::open_bootstrap_with` in `crates/inillucent-pool/src/file.rs` takes SHARED before it reads anything and keeps it for the rest of the open. `recovery::open_file_as` in `crates/inillucent-engine/src/recovery.rs` then writes under that SHARED lock: `inillucent_wal::truncate_after` trims the last log segment to where this process's scan stopped and deletes later segments, `database.checkpoint()` runs when the replay moved the page count, `resume_above_every_stamp` can checkpoint, and `ImportedDatabase::open_as` gives back the file's tail. SHARED is the lock readers hold, so a process opening a file while another process is in the middle of a read statement changes the file under that reader, and two processes opening at once can both fold.

It is narrow: it needs unfolded log with a moved page count and an overlapping reader. It could not be made to happen deterministically from the command line, because a writer holding EXCLUSIVE refuses the second open and a reader cannot hold SHARED across statements.

**To do.** Raise to EXCLUSIVE, with the busy wait, before the first of those writes, and refuse with busy when it is not granted, or skip the writes an open does not need. A change that took EXCLUSIVE for the whole open was tried and reverted, because it serialises every open behind every reader. Add a test that holds SHARED on the file from another handle and asserts the open changes no byte of the database or the log.

## Bug 21. Nikaya's database leaked a shared value page after a sync: "Page 211841: never used"

On 2026-09-28 the Nikaya database `J:\nikaya-data\nikaya.rdb` was recovered and REINDEXed, and `inillucent integrity-check` answered `ok` on it. The Nikaya server then ran on 1.0.33 plus the two fixes of that day for about 40 minutes: two Gmail syncs, the first of which failed in its embedding pass with `UNIQUE constraint failed: chunk_embedding.rowid` (the rowid bug fixed in 260b2278, where an insert after the newest rows were deleted took rowid 1), and one kill by Service Manager. A copy taken during a clean stop then failed `integrity-check` with `Page 211841: never used`. Page 211841 is a `BlobShared` page stamped at lsn 21258437440, which is during the failed sync. The free map calls it allocated and no tree reaches it. It was the only leaked page: the check now lists every one (82c5f195), and it listed only 211841. The page was given back to the free map with the server stopped, and `integrity-check` then answered `ok` with every row count unchanged, so the cause is still open but the database is clean.

Not reproduced by: a transaction inserting fifty 3,000 byte values and rolling back, three 5,000 byte values inserted and deleted by one process, and the same by a long lived process that is then killed before a checkpoint. The failing embedding pass inserted `VECTOR(768)` values into `chunk_embedding` inside a transaction that then rolled back on the constraint error, and the sync also cascaded deletes from `document` to `chunk` and `chunk_embedding`; one of those is the likely cause.

**To do.** Reproduce with a `VECTOR` column: a transaction that inserts vectors onto a fresh shared page and then fails on a constraint, and an `ON DELETE CASCADE` that deletes rows whose values are on shared pages. Fix the path that leaks, and give `integrity-check` a way to list every leaked page rather than the first.


## Bug 22. An `inillucent-core` test process, or `inillucent embed`, can crash at exit with `STATUS_STACK_BUFFER_OVERRUN` after an ONNX Runtime session was dropped

Found on 2026-09-29 while building `inillucent embed` (commit ed70d251). On Windows, a process that dropped an ONNX Runtime session (ONNX Runtime 1.22.0, CUDA build, installed with `setup-embeddings runtime --gpu`) and then exited crashed with `STATUS_STACK_BUFFER_OVERRUN` in about 1 run in 6, after all of its work was done and written. `inillucent embed` now parks finished sessions in a process static and never drops them, which gave 0 failures in 30 runs. The `inillucent-core` test binary still crashes at exit sometimes for the same reason, and `inillucent-testrun` retries it, so the crash does not show as a failure. The idle reaper in `crates/inillucent-core/src/residency.rs` drops sessions in long lived processes too, so a process that later exits may hit the same crash.

**To do.** Reproduce with a small program that opens an `OnnxEmbedder`, embeds once, drops it and exits, in a loop of 50 runs, on the CPU build and the CUDA build of the runtime. Find whether the crash is in ONNX Runtime teardown order (for example the environment released before a session) or in the `ort` crate, and fix it so a dropped session is safe. Then remove the parking in `crates/inillucent-cli/src/bulk_embed.rs` and the retry that hides it.

Priority: medium.

## Bug 23. Under heavy load, a multi process run lost an acknowledged commit and a reader saw a gap (`process_readers`)

Found on 2026-09-29 while releasing 2.0.1, in the merge cadence test run at commit b90f47d3 (engine code identical to 8528257c, whose run was green an hour earlier). `inillucent-compat::durability::process_readers` runs one writer process committing `n = 1..2000`, one row per transaction, checkpointing every 100 commits, beside four reader processes, with `locking_mode = normal`. Under the runner's 24 way parallel load both arms failed, and the suite took 89 s against 7 to 42 s normally:

- **default arm:** after the writer acknowledged 2,000 commits, a fresh handle read `count(*), max(n)` = `1999,2000`. One acknowledged row is missing from the middle, and `check()` on the file passed.
- **sqlite page size arm:** reader 1 saw 1262 rows with a highest `n` of 1263, 19 times. That is a state with a gap that never existed.

Not reproduced in isolation: 1 run alone, 8 runs with 28 CPU threads busy, and 10 runs beside `vacuum_crash`, `search_crash` and `process_campaign` with 16 CPU threads busy all passed. Two storage changes landed since the last green nightly (86b254e): encryption at rest (6c48a3cc) and `Pool::discard_all` putting each discarded frame back on the free list (1049dc7b), which runs when a connection resynchronises after another process writes. That is the path this test exercises, and it is how Nikaya runs (the server and the MCP server open one file).

**To do.** Reproduce it: run the suite in a loop inside the full `inillucent-testrun --cadence merge` load, or add a stress mode that repeats the writer and readers for many rounds. Check first whether `discard_all` can push a frame onto the free list that is still referenced (a swizzled pointer, a page table entry, or a frame already free), since two pages sharing a frame would lose a row exactly this way. Bisect between 1.0.33 and 2.0.1 once it reproduces.

Priority: high.

## Bug 24. `matrix` and `matrix_deep` shards write fixtures into the same scratch folder, so running both at once fails with a lost oracle or "no such table"

Found on 2026-09-30 at commit 31f100a3. `crates/inillucent-compat/src/statement_matrix/group.rs` builds each group's scratch folder as `CARGO_TARGET_TMPDIR/matrix/s{shard}/{family}-{group}-{arm}`. The tier is not in the path, so `inillucent-compat::matrix::insert` and `inillucent-compat::matrix_deep::insert` running shard 1 of the same group at the same time both use `tmp/matrix/s1/insert-1-default` and delete or rebuild each other's fixtures.

A `inillucent-testrun` run with `--target` for both `matrix::insert`, `matrix::expression`, `matrix_deep::insert` and `matrix_deep::expression` failed 5 targets with "the oracle could not open .../tmp/matrix/s1/insert-1-default/fixtures/.../sqlite.db: unable to open database file" and "inillucent failed and SQLite succeeded ... no such table: t0_ea05d3". Run one suite at a time, the same four targets all pass. A `--changed` run selects both tiers whenever a crate they cover changes, so it can fail this way on a change that has nothing to do with the SQL engine.

**To do.** Put the tier name (or the test binary's own name) in the scratch path, next to the shard number, and add a test that runs one group from both tiers at once.

Priority: medium.

title: Orphaned agent shells are accumulating at ~60/day and eating commit charge — find the leak, stop it, and reap the current backlog
description:
Found while diagnosing task-1766. Two jobs in one ticket: **reap the current backlog**, and **find and fix whatever is creating it** so it stops coming back.

## Why this matters

On task-1766 a MiniMax H3 render degraded ~100x (55 s/step to hours) because the host ran out of **commit charge**, not VRAM. The root cause there was a full C: shrinking the system-managed pagefile. But orphaned agent shells were holding **~7.6 GB** of commit at the same time, which on a box sitting at 10 GB free headroom is the difference between a render running at full speed and starving.

This is not tidiness. Free commit is the resource that decides whether a streaming render works.

## Measured backlog (2026-09-01 12:40Z)

Every one of these has a **dead parent process** — nothing is using them:

| process | orphaned | commit | oldest | newest |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `pwsh.exe` | **113** | 3.98 GB | 2026-08-30 16:05 | 2026-09-01 06:40 |
| `conhost.exe` | **126** | 0.18 GB | 2026-08-30 16:05 | 2026-09-01 06:57 |
| `claude.exe` | **10** | 3.41 GB | 2026-08-30 21:25 | 2026-08-30 22:20 |
| `cmd.exe` | **16** | 0.04 GB | 2026-08-29 21:49 | 2026-08-30 21:32 |
| **total** | **265** | **7.61 GB** | | |

Accrual rate for orphaned `pwsh` alone:

```
2026-08-30 : 60
2026-08-31 : 37
2026-09-01 : 16   (partial day)
```

**~60 per day, and still climbing** — the newest orphan was created minutes before this ticket was filed, so the leak is live, not historical. Note also 209 `conhost.exe` and 115 `pwsh.exe` total on the box; the orphans are most but not all of them.

## Investigation — where to look

The orphaned `pwsh.exe` have **no command-line arguments** (bare `pwsh.exe`) and their parents are gone. Candidates, roughly in order of suspicion:

1. **The agent PowerShell tool.** Each PowerShell tool call appears to spawn a host that is not reaped when the call returns. The 1:1-ish ratio of orphaned `conhost` to orphaned `pwsh` (126:113) is consistent with one console host per shell.
2. **Agent-terminal teardown.** `agent_done` reaps the PTY, and prior work already found that **`TaskStop` kills the shell but not its children** — so a reap that targets only the top process leaves grandchildren orphaned. The 10 orphaned `claude.exe` are all from a single window on the evening of 2026-08-30, which looks exactly like one batch of terminals being closed without their trees.
3. **The three terminal daemons** — Claude (8092), opencode (8093), Codex (8094) — and how they spawn and dispose of shells.
4. `/process-tasks` sprint runs, which launch a terminal per ticket. The repo already warns that a full board run leaves "dozens of stray Windows command processes".

Worth capturing during investigation: run one PowerShell tool call and one agent-terminal lifecycle in isolation and count `pwsh`/`conhost` before and after. That should identify the leak in minutes rather than by inference.

## Work

1. **Reap the current backlog** — the 265 processes above. Safety rules below are not optional.
2. **Find the leak** using the isolation test described above.
3. **Fix it at the source** so shells are disposed with their parents.
4. **Add a safety net**: a periodic sweeper that reaps dead-parented `pwsh`/`conhost`/`cmd` older than a few hours. Belongs alongside the existing system alarms.
5. **Consider a commit-headroom alarm** (see task-1768) so this class of problem is visible before it degrades a render.

## ⛔ Safety rules for the reap — do not deviate

- **Never `taskkill /IM`, `Stop-Process -Name`, or any kill-all of a process class.** There is a guard hook against kill-all-node for exactly this reason; it has taken prod, the Service Manager and other agents' sessions down before.
- **Only kill processes whose parent PID no longer exists.** Enumerate, verify the parent is dead, then `Stop-Process -Id <pid>` one at a time.
- **Never `/T` (tree-kill)** anything, and never touch the Service Manager — every service on the box is its child.
- **Do not kill a `claude.exe` belonging to a live session.** Verify it is orphaned AND that no terminal is attached before touching it.
- Leave the Service Manager, prod/dev backends, llama.cpp, ComfyUI, the terminal daemons, Nikaya and every registered service alone.
- Record free commit before and after so the reclaim is measured, not assumed.

## Context

- Parent ticket: **task-1766** (the "wedged GPU" — a commit-charge starvation misread as a GPU fault).
- Related: **task-1768** (surface commit headroom and s/step so this class is visible).
- On task-1766 the agent reaped only the 14 orphans it had created itself and left the other 110 alone, per the rule that an agent cleans up only what it started. This ticket is the authorisation to clear the rest.

title: unluminous mcp issues
description:
# Issues found driving Unluminous through the MCP tools

## What this records

An agent was asked to drive an Unluminous window entirely through the Model Context Protocol (MCP) tools:
write a JavaScript file that prints prime numbers, open it in a tab, run it, read the output, edit
it, save it and run it again. All of that worked. Five problems turned up while doing it, and this
document records them with the code that causes each one.

MCP is the protocol an agent uses to call tools in another program. Unluminous serves it through
`unluminous-cli`, which forwards each tool call to a running window over a loopback TCP connection.

The session used Unluminous 0.12.0, build date 2026-08-26 1:51pm, on macOS 26.5.1 (25F80), driving the
window on `/Users/jason.mcaffee/dev/unluminous-testing` (process 88081, port 64874). The source line
numbers below are from commit
[`db470c6`](https://github.com/jasonmcaffee/unluminous/commit/db470c66ef151f7a02991631fe3e7490a2bcdcb6).

## Jargon used below

| Term | What it means here |
| --- | --- |
| Frame loop | The single thread that draws the window. Unluminous answers every command from this thread, one command batch per drawn frame. |
| Semaphore | A lock a thread waits on until another thread signals it. A thread waiting on one is asleep and uses no processor time. |
| Occluded window | A window macOS has decided is not visible, because another window covers it. macOS stops asking an occluded window to draw. |
| `request_repaint` | The egui call that asks the window to draw another frame. It is how a background thread tells the window there is something to do. |
| Structured content | The machine readable JSON object in an MCP tool reply, as opposed to the human readable text block that accompanies it. |

## Issue 1: an idle window never drains the command queue, so every command times out

This is the one that makes driving Unluminous through MCP unreliable. Everything else in this document is
smaller.

### What happens

When the Unluminous window sits idle, every MCP tool call and every `unluminous-cli` command fails with
`timed-out: Unluminous did not answer <command> within 15000 ms`. The process is alive the whole time,
sleeping at 0% processor use, still listening on its port. It looks exactly like a hung application
and it is not hung.

Generating any user interface event fixes it instantly. This is the measurement, with `tab list`
called twice and nothing changed in between except bringing the window to the front:

**Evidence: two `unluminous-cli tab list` calls, before and after activating the window.**

```
--- before: Unluminous idle in the background ---
Unluminous did not answer tab.list within 15000 ms.     took 15.09s
--- activating the window with: open -b com.jasonmcaffee.unluminous ---
--- after: Unluminous frontmost ---
1 open                                              took 0.05s
```

Raising the timeout does not help. The MCP tool call accepts a `timeout` argument, and it is honoured
correctly, and the command still never gets answered:

**Evidence: the same `run list` tool call twice, with an idle window.**

```
mcp__unluminous__unluminous_run {"command": "list"}
  -> timed-out: Unluminous did not answer run.list within 15000 ms.

mcp__unluminous__unluminous_run {"command": "list", "arguments": {"timeout": 60000}}
  -> timed-out: Unluminous did not answer run.list within 65000 ms.
```

Sixty five seconds with an idle window and the queue was still not drained. So this is not a slow
frame that a longer deadline would cover.

### Why it happens

Every command is answered by the frame loop, which is the correct design and is written down as
such:

**Source:** [`unluminous`, `crates/unluminous-app/src/services/control.rs` lines 27 to 32](https://github.com/jasonmcaffee/unluminous/blob/db470c66ef151f7a02991631fe3e7490a2bcdcb6/crates/unluminous-app/src/services/control.rs#L27-L32)

```rust
//! ## Why the window answers rather than the thread
//!
//! Every command changes or reads the window's own state, and the window is a single thread with a
//! frame loop. So the listener does not touch it: it queues the request, wakes the window, and
//! waits for the answer. The window drains the queue at the top of a frame, which is also what
//! makes a command's effect visible in the very next screenshot.
```

The connection thread queues the request, calls `wake()`, and then waits:

**Source:** [`unluminous`, `crates/unluminous-app/src/services/control.rs` lines 285 to 298](https://github.com/jasonmcaffee/unluminous/blob/db470c66ef151f7a02991631fe3e7490a2bcdcb6/crates/unluminous-app/src/services/control.rs#L285-L298)

```rust
    let command = request.command.clone();
    let (answer, wait) = mpsc::channel();
    if sender.send(Pending { request, reply: Some(answer) }).is_err() {
        return Reply::failed(&command, code::NOT_RUNNING, "Unluminous is closing.");
    }
    wake();
    match wait.recv_timeout(BACKSTOP) {
        Ok(reply) => reply,
        Err(_) => Reply::failed(
            &command,
            code::TIMED_OUT,
            "Unluminous did not answer. The window may be busy or may have stopped drawing.",
        ),
    }
```

`wake` is `request_repaint` on the egui context:

**Source:** [`unluminous`, `crates/unluminous-app/src/app/mod.rs` lines 689 to 695](https://github.com/jasonmcaffee/unluminous/blob/db470c66ef151f7a02991631fe3e7490a2bcdcb6/crates/unluminous-app/src/app/mod.rs#L689-L695)

```rust
    pub fn open_control_channel(&mut self, ctx: &egui::Context) {
        let folder = self.tree.root().to_path_buf();
        // The context rather than `thread_waker`, because this is called before the first frame and
        // the window has not yet been given one to wake.
        let context = ctx.clone();
        self.control =
            control::Server::start(folder, Arc::new(move || context.request_repaint()));
```

`request_repaint` asks for a frame. It cannot make macOS draw a window macOS has decided not to
draw. When the window is occluded or otherwise idle, the request is recorded, no frame is drawn, the
queue is never drained, and the waiting connection thread sleeps until its deadline.

Process stacks taken with `sample 88081` while four commands were stuck confirm this exactly. Four
threads named `unluminous-control-connection` were each parked on the semaphore inside
`unluminous_app::services::control::serve`:

**Evidence: `sample 88081`, one of four identical `unluminous-control-connection` threads.**

```
2495 Thread_13934062: unluminous-control-connection
  2495 unluminous_app::services::control::serve  (in unluminous) + 1936
    2495 _dispatch_semaphore_wait_slow  (in libdispatch.dylib) + 76
      2495 _dispatch_sema4_timedwait  (in libdispatch.dylib) + 64
        2495 semaphore_timedwait_trap  (in libsystem_kernel.dylib) + 8
```

At the same moment the frame loop was parked in its ordinary event wait, with no frame pending:

**Evidence: `sample 88081`, the main thread during the same stall.**

```
2495 Thread_13910223   DispatchQueue_1: com.apple.main-thread  (serial)
  2495 -[NSApplication run]  (in AppKit) + 368
    2495 _DPSNextEvent  (in AppKit) + 576
      2495 __CFRunLoopServiceMachPort  (in CoreFoundation) + 160
        2495 mach_msg2_trap  (in libsystem_kernel.dylib) + 8
```

The comment on the backstop constant already anticipates this state, which suggests it was known to
be possible but was treated as something only a broken window would reach:

**Source:** [`unluminous`, `crates/unluminous-app/src/services/control.rs` lines 49 to 54](https://github.com/jasonmcaffee/unluminous/blob/db470c66ef151f7a02991631fe3e7490a2bcdcb6/crates/unluminous-app/src/services/control.rs#L49-L54)

```rust
/// How long the listener will hold a connection open waiting for the window to answer.
///
/// Longer than any command's own wait, because the command's own timeout is the one that should
/// fire and say what it was waiting for. This is the backstop for a window that has stopped drawing
/// altogether, which would otherwise leave the caller hanging for ever.
const BACKSTOP: Duration = Duration::from_secs(120);
```

An idle window is a normal window, not a broken one. An agent driving Unluminous produces exactly this
state, because between two tool calls nothing touches the keyboard or the mouse.

### Suggested fix

Stop making a drawn frame the only thing that drains the queue. Three options, in the order worth
trying:

1. Have the wake send a winit user event through an `EventLoopProxy` rather than only asking egui for
   a repaint, and drain the queue when that user event is handled. A user event wakes the event loop
   whether or not macOS wants to draw the window.
2. While any request is outstanding, set the winit control flow to `Poll` so the event loop keeps
   turning and the queue keeps being drained.
3. Answer the commands that only read state on the connection thread, behind a lock, so reading
   state never depends on the window drawing. This is the largest change of the three and it gives up
   the property that a command's effect shows in the very next screenshot.

Whichever is chosen, a test should cover it: queue a command while the window is not drawing frames
and assert that it is still answered.

## Issue 2: a run configuration that cannot start is reported as a success

### What happens

The first attempt at running the prime numbers file used a run configuration whose command was
`node primes.js`. Unluminous spawns without a shell, and a window launched from Finder does not have the
nvm directory on its `PATH`, so `node` could not be found. Through MCP the failure was invisible.
This is the whole reply the agent received:

**Evidence: the MCP reply to `run start` for a program that does not exist.**

```json
{"activeRun":"primes","configurations":[
  {"command":"definitely-not-a-real-program","directory":"","env":"","exitCode":null,
   "name":"bogus","origin":"permanent","running":false,"started":false,"state":null}],
 "height":260,"runs":["primes"],"selected":"bogus","visible":false}
```

`started` is `false`, `state` is `null`, and there is no reason given anywhere. The call is not
marked as an error. The same command through `unluminous-cli` prints the reason:

**Evidence: `unluminous-cli run start primes` with `node` not on the window's PATH.**

```
Unluminous could not start node: Failed to spawn command 'node': No such file or directory (os error 2)
```

An agent holding only the structured content cannot tell why nothing ran, and cannot tell the
difference between a program that failed to spawn and a program that ran and exited immediately.

### Why it happens

The failure text is put into the window's status bar message:

**Source:** [`unluminous`, `crates/unluminous-app/src/app/mod.rs` lines 1563 to 1570](https://github.com/jasonmcaffee/unluminous/blob/db470c66ef151f7a02991631fe3e7490a2bcdcb6/crates/unluminous-app/src/app/mod.rs#L1563-L1570)

```rust
        match self.run.start(configuration, &root, size, waker) {
            Ok(_) => {
                self.show_the_run_tile(true);
                self.focus = Focus::Terminal;
                self.message = Some(format!("Running {name}"));
            }
            Err(problem) => self.message = Some(problem),
        }
```

`cli_run_do` then reads that status bar message and returns `ok` regardless of whether the run
started:

**Source:** [`unluminous`, `crates/unluminous-app/src/app/cli.rs` lines 2927 to 2930](https://github.com/jasonmcaffee/unluminous/blob/db470c66ef151f7a02991631fe3e7490a2bcdcb6/crates/unluminous-app/src/app/cli.rs#L2927-L2930)

```rust
        self.message = None;
        self.run_a_configuration(what(named));
        let said = self.message.clone().unwrap_or_default();
        ok(request, said, self.run_value())
```

Because `reply.error` is never set, the MCP layer takes the success path, marks `isError` false, and
attaches the structured content that a client will render in preference to the text:

**Source:** [`unluminous`, `unluminous-cli/src/mcp/server.rs` lines 181 to 195](https://github.com/jasonmcaffee/unluminous/blob/db470c66ef151f7a02991631fe3e7490a2bcdcb6/unluminous-cli/src/mcp/server.rs#L181-L195)

```rust
    /// Turn what the window said into what an agent reads.
    fn tool_result(&self, command: &'static Command, reply: &Reply) -> Value {
        if let Some(failure) = &reply.error {
            return refused(format!("{}: {}", failure.code, failure.message));
        }
        let mut content = vec![json!({ "type": "text", "text": spoken(reply) })];
        if let Some(picture) = self.picture_from(command, reply) {
            content.push(picture);
        }
        let mut answer = json!({ "content": content, "isError": false });
        if !reply.result.is_null() {
            answer["structuredContent"] = reply.result.clone();
        }
        answer
    }
```

### Suggested fix

Make `run_a_configuration` report whether it started, and have `cli_run_do` return `no(request,
code::FAILED, problem)` when it did not. That sets `reply.error`, which makes the MCP layer return a
refusal carrying the real reason, and makes the `unluminous-cli` exit code correct at the same time.

Separately, a run configuration whose program cannot be found is worth catching earlier. `run add`
accepts `node primes.js` without complaint and the problem only appears at `run start`. Resolving
the program against `PATH` at `run add` time and saying so when it cannot be found would remove the
most likely first failure an agent hits, because an agent will write `node`, `python` or `cargo` and
those are exactly the programs a version manager keeps off a Finder launched application's `PATH`.

## Issue 3: a command that reports a timeout has usually already been applied

### What happens

Because of the idle window problem in Issue 1, the client gives up while the request is still sitting
in the queue. The window then drains it later, when something wakes it. The command takes effect
after the caller has been told it failed.

Three commands in this session reported `timed-out` over MCP and all three had in fact been applied:

- `run add bogus` reported a timeout. The configuration was in
  `.unluminous/run-configurations.conf` as `run.3` afterwards.
- `run remove bogus` reported a timeout. The configuration was gone afterwards.
- `run rerun primes` reported a timeout. The program had run, the state was `finished`, and the
  output was there.

An agent that retries a command after a timeout will apply it twice. For `run add` that is harmless.
For `editor insert`, `tab close --discard` or `explorer delete` it is not.

### Why it happens

The client deadline is shorter than the window's own backstop, so the client abandons a request the
window will still honour. The client default is 15 seconds:

**Source:** [`unluminous`, `unluminous-cli/src/client.rs` line 16](https://github.com/jasonmcaffee/unluminous/blob/db470c66ef151f7a02991631fe3e7490a2bcdcb6/unluminous-cli/src/client.rs#L16)

```rust
pub const DEFAULT_TIMEOUT: Duration = Duration::from_millis(15_000);
```

The window's backstop is 120 seconds, so there is a window of 105 seconds in which the caller has
been told the command failed and the command has not been cancelled.

### Suggested fix

Fixing Issue 1 removes almost all of these. On top of that, the queued request should be cancelled
when the caller goes away, so a timeout means the command did not happen. The connection thread
already owns the `Pending`; it should mark it abandoned when `recv_timeout` fires, and the frame loop
should discard an abandoned request instead of running it. Until that exists, the timeout message
should say plainly that the command may still be applied, because the current wording reads as a
failure.

## Issue 4: a stalled command blocks the screenshot needed to diagnose it

### What happens

`window screenshot` is the tool the MCP server instructions recommend for seeing what a command
actually did, and it travels over the same channel as everything else. During the stall in Issue 1 it
timed out along with the rest, so the one tool that would show what the window was doing was
unavailable exactly when it was needed. Diagnosis had to fall back on the macOS `screencapture`
command and on `sample` to read the process stacks, neither of which an agent driving Unluminous would
normally reach for.

Four connection threads were stuck at once, each holding a thread for its full deadline.

### Suggested fix

This mostly follows from fixing Issue 1. Two things would still help on their own. Answer `status`
and `window screenshot` without waiting on a frame, from the last frame's state, so that an agent can
always find out what the window thinks is happening. And include in the timeout reply whatever the
server already knows, such as how many requests are queued and when the last frame was drawn, so a
caller can tell a busy window from one that has stopped drawing.

## Issue 5: the MCP tool descriptions do not mention the arguments that control waiting

### What happens

The MCP tool schemas take a free form `arguments` object and describe it as "the values the command
takes, by the name in its usage line". The usage lines cover each command's own arguments. They do
not mention that `timeout` is accepted on every call, because `timeout` is a global flag of the
command line interface rather than part of any usage line:

**Source:** [`unluminous`, `unluminous-cli/src/parse.rs` line 85](https://github.com/jasonmcaffee/unluminous/blob/db470c66ef151f7a02991631fe3e7490a2bcdcb6/unluminous-cli/src/parse.rs#L85)

```rust
    ("timeout", Some("milliseconds"), "How long to wait for an answer. 15000 by default."),
```

It is accepted, and the MCP driver reads it and adds five seconds of headroom:

**Source:** [`unluminous`, `unluminous-cli/src/mcp/driver.rs` lines 205 to 214](https://github.com/jasonmcaffee/unluminous/blob/db470c66ef151f7a02991631fe3e7490a2bcdcb6/unluminous-cli/src/mcp/driver.rs#L205-L214)

```rust
/// How long to wait for this call.
fn timeout_for(arguments: &Map<String, Value>) -> Duration {
    let waiting = ["timeout", "wait"]
        .iter()
        .filter_map(|name| arguments.get(*name))
        .filter_map(as_millis)
        .max()
        .unwrap_or(0);
    DEFAULT_TIMEOUT.max(Duration::from_millis(waiting + 5_000))
}
```

The agent only discovered `timeout` by reading this source. Note also that `DEFAULT_TIMEOUT.max(...)`
means 15 seconds is a floor: a caller can raise the deadline but cannot lower it, so an agent that
wants to fail fast cannot.

### Suggested fix

Say in each tool's description that `timeout` in milliseconds is accepted on any call. If a caller
should be able to fail faster than 15 seconds, use the passed value directly rather than taking the
maximum of it and the default.

## One note about the setup, which is not an Unluminous bug

The agent that found all of this was running inside the Unluminous window it was driving. The parent chain
was Unluminous (process 88081) to `/bin/zsh` to `claude` to the shell each command ran in, and the hosting
terminal tab was named "Unluminous MCP UI driving".

That matters for anyone reproducing this. Restarting Unluminous to clear the stall destroys the session
doing the testing, which happened once before the session that produced this document. Recover with
a user interface event instead. To test anything that needs a restart, start a second window with
`unluminous-cli launch <folder>` and drive it with the `instance` argument.

It also affects how the stall presents. A Claude Code session draws an animated spinner in its
terminal, and that animation keeps waking the frame loop, so commands are fast for as long as the
agent is producing output and start timing out once the terminal goes quiet. That is why the problem
looks intermittent when it is not.

title: Unluminous: screenshots test binary crashes at teardown (0xc0000005), failing ~40% of full-workspace test runs
description:
Found while supervising task-1649 and task-1652. Not a defect in either ticket — filing separately because it makes Unluminous's test suite unusable as a gate.

## What happens

`cargo test --workspace --release` in `C:\jason\dev\unluminous` fails roughly **2 runs in 5**, like this:

```
error: test failed, to rerun pass `-p unluminous-app --test screenshots`

Caused by:
  process didn't exit successfully: `target\release\deps\screenshots-<hash>.exe`
  (exit code: 0xc0000005, STATUS_ACCESS_VIOLATION)
note: test exited abnormally
```

**Every one of the 91 screenshot tests has already printed `ok` when this happens.** The crash is at process teardown, after the last test and before the harness prints its `test result:` line — so cargo reports the entire workspace as failed while listing 91 passes and zero failures. That is a confusing thing to hand someone, and on a CI run it would read as a real regression.

## Measurements

- 5 full-workspace runs tonight → **2 crashed** at teardown, 3 clean at 487 then 489 passing.
- `cargo test -p unluminous-app --test screenshots --release` in isolation → **clean every time**, 91/91, exit 0 (3 runs).
- So it needs the full-workspace run to reproduce, which points at teardown racing something rather than at any individual test.

Access violation in a test binary that renders through wgpu points at GPU/device teardown — the harness tearing down a wgpu device or surface while something still holds it, or two test binaries' GPU contexts overlapping as one process exits and the next starts.

## Suggested direction

Reproduce under a debugger or with `RUST_BACKTRACE=full` and `--no-capture` to get the faulting frame; check whether the kittest/egui-wgpu harness leaves a device alive at exit and whether an explicit drop or a `Instance::poll_all` before exit settles it. If it turns out to be unfixable from our side, running the screenshots target as its own step is a workaround — but establish the cause first, because a 40% crash rate at teardown may well be a real lifetime bug rather than test-only noise.

## Not urgent, but not cosmetic

Nothing ships wrong to a user. The cost is that `cargo test --workspace` cannot currently be trusted to mean what it says.

title: The update check asks a private repository, so it answers 404 to every user but you
description:
Found while open-sourcing Unluminous on task-1989. It is not from that ticket — the code is unchanged — but making the source public is what makes it visible, and the installer on unluminous.com has been handing this to strangers since 0.49.0.

`crates/unluminous-app/src/services/update.rs` asks:

```
const RELEASES: &str = "https://api.github.com/repos/jasonmcaffee/unluminous/releases/latest";
pub const RELEASES_PAGE: &str = "https://github.com/jasonmcaffee/unluminous/releases";
```

Both name `jasonmcaffee/unluminous`, which is **private**. Measured with no credential:

| what | anonymous |
|---|---|
| `api.github.com/repos/jasonmcaffee/unluminous/releases/latest` | **404** |
| `github.com/jasonmcaffee/unluminous/releases` | **404** |
| `api.github.com/repos/Black-Rainbow-Labs/Unluminous/releases` | 200, **0 releases** |

So for anybody who installed Unluminous from unluminous.com:

- `Unluminous -> Check for Updates` cannot ever find one, and `unluminous-cli update check` cannot either. The module's own comment says the feature exists because *"this is the largest single gap between 'we shipped a fix' and 'someone has the fix'"* — and for every user but Jason the gap is total.
- `RELEASES_PAGE` is the URL the refusal hands back and the one `plugins`/`settings` reports as `url`, so a person told "go and get it" is sent to a 404.
- Turning `update.check` on to `start` — the one thing the Settings page offers — makes the window ask a URL that 404s on every launch.

Nothing is silently wrong in the sense of a bad answer: the check fails and says so. What is wrong is that it can never succeed, and the setting invites somebody to switch on a request that cannot work.

**This needs a decision rather than a patch**, which is why task-1989 measured it and changed nothing:

1. **Cut GitHub releases on `Black-Rainbow-Labs/Unluminous`** and point both constants there. That is the shape the code already has, and it makes the releases page a real page. It means publishing the installer as a release asset in two places, since unluminous.com hosts its own copy.
2. **Ask unluminous.com instead.** The site is already the distribution point and already holds the version, the size and the SHA-256 in `SITE`. It would need a small JSON manifest — there is none today — and `RELEASES_PAGE` would become `https://unluminous.com/#install`.
3. **Withdraw the check** rather than ship one that cannot work, and leave `Unluminous -> Check for Updates` saying where to look.

(2) is the one that matches where the bytes actually are. (1) is the one that needs the least code.

Related: `unluminous-site/scripts/sync-release.mjs` and `blackrainbowlabs/scripts/sync-release.mjs` both read releases from the same private repository, which is why the Black Rainbow Labs page still shows Unluminous `v0.37.1`. Whichever answer is chosen here should settle those too.

title: Retiring a worktree leaves a .cargo/config.toml that silently redirects later builds
description:
Found while working task-2059.

`POST /tasks/:id/worktree/retire` removes the junctions, the worktree and the branch, but it can leave files behind in `<repo>/.claude/worktrees/task-<N>/`. After task-2059's first worktree was retired, that directory still held:

- `.cargo/config.toml` — written by the backend when the worktree was created, pointing `target-dir` at `D:/agent-worktrees/cargo-target/agent-tasks-service-task-2059`
- `app.rdb` and `app.rdb-wal.0000000001` — untracked files a test run inside the worktree had produced

**The `.cargo/config.toml` is the damaging one, because cargo reads it from the WORKING directory's hierarchy rather than the manifest's.** An agent terminal whose shell is still sitting in that directory — which is exactly where a session lands after its own worktree is retired — runs

```
cargo build --release --manifest-path C:/jason/dev/<some other repo>/Cargo.toml
```

and gets `Finished `release` profile [optimized] target(s)`. The build really happened, into the scratch directory the stale config names. The other repository's executable is untouched. There is no error, no warning, and the only way to notice is to check the executable's timestamp afterwards.

On task-2059 this produced a wrong conclusion about a service restart: a rebuild of `dynamic-dns-updater` reported success while the running service kept a binary from a fortnight earlier, and it was only caught by an `ls` that showed the old date.

**What to change** (in `backend/src/services/worktree.service.ts`, the retire path):

1. Remove `.cargo/config.toml` and the `.cargo` directory when retiring, since the backend is what wrote them.
2. title: Unluminous: terminal send and read cannot target a tab, and the area has four conventions
description:
From the task-1695 observation study.

The agent made a new terminal tab, named it `checks`, and then wrote `{"command":"send","text":"cargo check","tab":1}` — and was refused: *"terminal send has no tab. terminal send takes text, no-enter, key."*

One area, four ways of naming a tab:

| verb | how a tab is named |
|---|---|
| `rename`, `move` | `--tab <index>` |
| `close`, `select` | a positional |
| **`send`, `read`** | **cannot — always "the tab that is showing"** |

The two verbs where targeting matters most are the two that lack it. `terminal select` then `terminal send` is two calls where one would do, and between them anything else driving the window can change which tab is showing — so it is a race, not just a round trip. An agent running a build in one tab and a dev server in another has no safe way to speak to either.

**Scope**
- `terminal send` and `terminal read` take `--tab <index>`, defaulting to the tab that is showing, so nothing that works today changes.
- Settle one convention for naming a tab across the area and make the other verbs accept it too, keeping what already works.
- Tests that send to a tab that is not showing and read it back without selecting it.

**How to work it**: research online, write a TDD, implement fully, verify against a real window with two terminal tabs running different things.

Evidence: `FINDINGS.md` and `sessions/s06-terminal.md`, `s22-multifile.md`.

title: NInfer: set it up, benchmark it against llama.cpp, and publish a Labs page
description:
Evaluate **NInfer** as an alternative inference engine for Qwen 3.8-27B on this box, and publish the results as a Labs page.

## Why this is worth doing

NInfer is a from-scratch C++/CUDA inference engine written specifically for Qwen 3.6/3.8 checkpoints on an RTX 5090. Its own published head-to-head against llama.cpp claims **+43% decode at 128k and +60% at 200k**, with the prefill crossover just under a 64k prompt. Field reports on r/LocalLLaMA are stronger still: **170-200 tok/s single stream and ~6,500 tok/s prefill at a 260k context**, and one user running it with Claude Code reported roughly double their llama.cpp speed on a real repo.

For comparison, task-1598 measured our best llama.cpp configuration (Qwen3.8-27B UD-Q6_K across both 5090s, `-sm tensor`, 262k window, b10507) at **106.5 / 99.0 / 86.5 tok/s** at 2k / 150k / 250k depth. If NInfer's numbers hold on this hardware it is a large win for the coding agent lane.

## Two things to establish up front, because they decide whether it can ever ship here

1. **It is single-GPU by design** — "one RTX 5090, one CUDA device", one resident sequence, one active request. So it cannot use the second card, and everything it does has to be judged against the *single-GPU* llama.cpp baseline as well as the two-GPU one.
2. **It is an int4-class engine** (groupwise-int weights, INT8 group-64 KV). task-1598's research found the field reporting that Qwen 3.8's long-chain reasoning degrades below 5 bits and loops on a quantized KV cache, which is exactly why our coder config is Q6. **So the headline question is not "is it faster" — it is "is it faster AND still good at xhigh reasoning".** Speed alone does not clear the bar this studio sets.

## What to do

**1. Research and install.** Start from `github.com/Neroued/ninfer` (there are per-GPU forks — `ninfer-5090`, `ninfer-4090`, `ninfer3090` — check which is current for a 5090). Work out how checkpoints are compiled to its `.ninfer` format and what that costs in disk and time. Register it as a Service Manager service, on its own port, `autoRestart: false`, **stopped by default** — it must not compete with the existing llama.cpp server.

**2. Benchmark it head to head, on the same harness.** Reuse `_agent_output/task-1598-2gpu-qwen/` (`run-sweep.cjs`, `bench.cjs`, `ceiling.cjs`, `summarize.cjs`, `pcie-sample.cjs`) so the numbers are directly comparable to task-1598's rather than a fresh set that only compares to itself. It is OpenAI-compatible, so `bench.cjs` should point at it with little change. Measure:
   - decode tok/s at **2k / 50k / 150k / 250k** depth, medians of at least 5;
   - prefill tok/s at those depths, and a genuine **cold full prefill** (task-1598's prefill column is an incremental rate because `cache_prompt` is on — do not repeat that ambiguity without labelling it);
   - **max on-GPU context** (does it really reach 262k on one card, and does it refuse past the trained window the way llama.cpp does?);
   - VRAM and host RAM;
   - **PCIe replay delta per arm** — it runs on one card, so which card matters: GPU 1's link is faulty (task-1396).

**3. Judge quality, not just speed.** This is the part that decides it. Run its int4 weights against our Q6 llama.cpp config on the same prompts at **xhigh reasoning**, and look for the failure the field describes: reasoning loops, degraded long-chain tool use, truncation. A perplexity number alone is not enough — task-1554 already showed PPL is flat from Q4_K_XL up while behaviour is not.

**4. Publish a Labs page.** Add it to the Labs section (`ui/src/app/labs/`, following `Qwen38Gallery.tsx` as the pattern). It must carry **real measured numbers and charts**, not prose claims: the depth/throughput comparison against both llama.cpp baselines, the context ceiling, VRAM, and a plain verdict on the quality question. Say what we would actually adopt and under what conditions.

## Definition of done

- NInfer installed, registered as a stopped-by-default service, and serving Qwen 3.8-27B.
- A measured head-to-head against task-1598's llama.cpp numbers on the same harness, at matching depths.
- A quality verdict at xhigh reasoning, with evidence.
- A Labs page published with the numbers and charts.
- A recommendation: adopt / adopt-for-X-only / reject, with the reason.
- Nothing that currently serves the studio changed as a side effect. If NInfer wins, propose the change; do not silently switch anything.

## Cleanup

Compiled `.ninfer` checkpoints are large. Record where they came from and how to rebuild them, and delete any losing candidates when the study is finished.

title: Guard the commit ceiling: a full C: silently starves H3 renders by 100x, and nothing warns
description:
From task-1766 ("the wedged GPU"). Root cause is confirmed and the immediate incident is resolved; this ticket is about making the box resilient to it and making it visible when it happens.

> **History:** this ticket was filed twice against the wrong cause — first an attached LoRA, then llama.cpp's residency. Jason rejected both on the same correct grounds: neither had changed, so neither could explain a new failure. The version below is the measured cause.

## What happened

A MiniMax H3 render at 1536x832 / 362 frames was on course for **~45 hours**. The identical request completes in **~25 minutes**. Nothing about the render, the LoRA, the GPU, the ComfyUI version or any service's configuration had changed.

**What changed was the disk.** C: reached 99% full (58 GB free of 3.7 TB). The pagefile is system-managed and lives on C:, and Windows sizes it from available space — so it sat pinned at 56 GB and could never grow:

```
  physical RAM     127.5 GB
+ pagefile          56.0 GB   <- could not grow; C: was full
= COMMIT LIMIT     183.5 GB
  commit in use    179.9 GB
  HEADROOM            3.6 GB
```

A streaming H3 render needs ~20 GB of host-side staging on top of what ComfyUI already holds. With 3.6 GB of headroom there is nowhere for it to come from, the staging path degrades, and the GPU starves: 100% "utilisation" at ~130 W instead of 575 W, and a 55-second sampling step becomes hours.

It is a **gradient, not a switch** — the same render took 57.5 min the day before (`ui_videos` 1194) and 27.9 min on a healthy box. The degradation tracked C: filling up.

## Proof (task-1766)

Pressure applied and removed **inside one running render**, so everything else is constant by construction:

| step | free commit | s/step | GPU power |
|---|---|---|---|
| 2-4 | ~39 GB | **55.4-55.8** | 575-578 W |
| 5 | **5.1 GB** | **219** | **134 W** |
| 6 | **2.3 GB** | **421** | **210 W** |
| 7 | 29.7 GB | 81 | 569 W |
| 8-10 | 36-41 GB | **55.7-55.8** | 570-576 W |

55 -> 421 -> 55 s/step, driven only by host commit headroom.

## Ruled out by measurement

| Candidate | Verdict |
|---|---|
| The attached LoRA (`h3\HMNSFW_AIO_V2`, 208 patches) | **Cleared.** ~0.1 s/step; one-off ~356 s at staging |
| llama.cpp being resident | **Cleared as a cause.** It has always run during H3 renders. It contributes to commit demand, but the ceiling is the fault. **Do not add a rule that stops llama.** |
| Transcribe Audio on `cudaDevice 0` | **Not this incident** — longstanding config. See tidy-up below. |
| Clip length / canvas | **Cleared.** Same canvas + length completes in 27.9 min |
| GPU / PCIe link | **Cleared.** gen5 x16, 0 replays, full clocks, no throttling |
| SageAttention int32 ceiling | **Not reached.** 136,502 tokens vs the 299,592 limit |
| ComfyUI 0.33.0 vs 0.34.0 | **Not the cause** — the incident reproduced on 0.34.0 |

## Already done (task-1766)

- Jason freed **1.36 TB** on C:.
- ComfyUI restarted, returning the **58.5 GB** it had accumulated: commit free 3.6 GB -> 58.2 GB, **with llama left running**.
- ComfyUI 0.33.0 -> 0.34.0, llama.cpp b10507 -> b10733.

## Work this ticket asks for

1. **Resize the pagefile now that C: has room** (needs elevation, one-off, then a reboot). 128 GB initial / 256 GB max takes the commit limit from 183.5 GB to ~255 GB. Windows does **not** resize a system-managed pagefile retroactively, so freeing the disk alone does not fix it.
2. **Alarm on low commit headroom.** task-1556 added `/system/kernel-pool`; extend that idea. Below ~20 GB of free commit the box cannot run a streaming H3 render at speed, and today nothing says so. This is the highest-value guard because it catches the whole class, not just this instance.
3. **Show measured s/step and a projected finish while a render is in flight.** During the incident the Videos page said `Sampling - 10%, ~25 min left` for a job heading to ~45 hours, with nothing on screen that would ever correct it (screenshot: `_agent_output/task-1766-gpu-wedge-upgrade/prod-videos-page.png`). The tqdm timings already exist in the Service Manager's captured ComfyUI stdout.
4. **Restart ComfyUI when its held memory grows past a threshold.** It accumulated 58.5 GB over a day; a restart returns all of it. This is task-1533's documented rule and nothing enforces it. Prefer this over any rule that stops other services.
5. **Tidy-up, low priority:** the Service Manager pins `Transcribe Audio` to `cudaDevice 0` (ComfyUI's card) while its own sidecar defaults to `GPU_DEVICE=1`. It did not cause this, but GPU 1 is where it belongs, alongside llama and Nikaya Embeddings.

## Constraints — do not undo settled decisions

- **Do not add a rule that stops `Llama.cpp Server` before a render.** It has always run during H3 renders and must keep doing so.
- Keep any advisory **advisory**. Capping H3 duration or resolution was QA-rejected on task-1519.
- **Do not** reintroduce a "quiet too long" watchdog timer (task-1539).
- **Do not** propose fewer steps, a turbo/distillation LoRA, or EasyCache (task-1496).
- **Do not** put `--disable-dynamic-vram` back (task-1539).

## Pointers

- `backend/src/workflows/createMinimaxH3VideoWorkflow.ts` - the H3 cost advisory
- `backend/src/controllers/videoCreation.controller.ts` - `GET /videos/minimax-h3/render-cost`
- ComfyUI `comfy/model_management.py` - `MAX_PINNED_MEMORY = ram * 0.40` (~51 GB here; no sizing flag, only `--disable-pinned-memory`)
- Raw evidence: `_agent_output/task-1766-gpu-wedge-upgrade/RESULTS.md`

description:
Reported live: 1920x1080, SageAttention only, 10s, 25 steps sat at 1% for 55 minutes with the GPU pinned at 100%.

Not a wedge and not a crash. ComfyUI loaded the text encoder (14,960 MB) and the video VAE (4,966 MB)
COMPLETELY and then did not unload them ("0 models unloaded"). The 1920x1088/243f activation reserve took

title: Fix Phone Sync / Proxy socket-buffer RAM leak (AfdB kernel pool)
description:
On 2026-08-16 the box hit 123/127.5 GB RAM with process working sets summing to only 54 GB — the missing 54 GB was kernel nonpaged pool, tag AfdB (Winsock socket buffers). Root cause: the Phone Sync server (127.0.0.1:7071) had died/been replaced, and the Proxy (C:/jason/dev/proxy, ai.jasonmcaffee.com) kept 257 upstream loopback connections to the DEAD instance. The orphaned sockets sat in FinWait1 with ~210 MB of undrained stream data pinned per pair. Loopback TCP windows grow huge, so per-socket kernel buffering is effectively unbounded. Restarting the Proxy freed all 54 GB instantly (nonpaged 56.9 → 2.7 GB).

Fix wanted so it cannot recur:
1. Proxy: destroy/timeout upstream connections when the client goes away or the upstream stops reading — an idle/half-close timeout on proxied streams (esp. long-lived phone-sync media streams), and cap per-connection buffering.
2. Phone Sync server: investigate why its old instance died leaving streams half-open, and make it close long-lived sync streams cleanly on shutdown/replace.
3. Optional guard: a periodic check that alerts when Memory\Pool Nonpaged Bytes exceeds ~8 GB, pointing at the AfdB diagnosis steps (pool-tag query via NtQuerySystemInformation SystemPoolTagInformation=22 — script pattern saved in the task-1554 session scratchpad as pooltags.ps1).

Diagnosis details and the exact recovery procedure are recorded in memory (project_afdb_socket_buffer_ram_leak_proxy) and in task-1554 comments.
